query: CoreWeave acquisitions Core Scientific Weights and Biases
normalized: acquisitions biases core coreweave scientific weights

output.content:
**CoreWeave’s two notable 2025 acquisition transactions had very different outcomes:** it completed the purchase of AI-development-platform company Weights & Biases, while its proposed all-stock acquisition of data-center operator Core Scientific was rejected by Core Scientific shareholders and terminated. [[1, 2]]

| Target | Announcement / completion | Consideration | Outcome and strategic rationale |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| **Weights & Biases** | Agreement announced in early March 2025; completed **May 5, 2025**. | Terms were not officially disclosed; press reporting cited a **$1.7 billion** price, attributed to The Information. [[3, 4]]| **Completed.** W&B’s experiment tracking, model evaluation, and developer workflow tools augment CoreWeave’s AI-compute infrastructure; CoreWeave said the combined offering would support building, deploying, and iterating AI models faster. [[1]]|
| **Core Scientific** | Definitive agreement announced **July 7, 2025**; proposed closing was Q4 2025. [[5]]| All-stock, fixed exchange ratio of **0.1235 CoreWeave Class A share per Core Scientific share**; implied equity value was about **$9.0 billion** as of July 3, 2025, or **$20.40 per CORZ share** and a stated 66% premium to the unaffected June 25 price. [[5]]| **Terminated October 30, 2025**, after Core Scientific stockholders did not approve the merger. Core Scientific remained Nasdaq-listed as **CORZ**, although the companies said they would continue their commercial partnership. [[6, 2]]|

**Weights & Biases: completed software-stack expansion.** CoreWeave acquired W&B to add an AI developer platform to its GPU-cloud infrastructure, while stating that W&B would remain interoperable across deployment options, infrastructure providers, foundation models, frameworks, and protocols. [[1]] W&B is now a CoreWeave product within **CoreWeave Forge**, providing tools to track experiments, evaluate models, and improve them. [[7]]

**Core Scientific: attempted vertical integration, but no ownership acquisition.** The proposed deal would have brought Core Scientific’s data-center footprint and approximately **1.3 GW of gross power**, plus over **1 GW** of potential expansion capacity, under CoreWeave ownership. [[5]] CoreWeave projected that acquiring rather than leasing the relevant sites would eliminate more than **$10 billion** of cumulative future lease overhead over 12 years and generate an estimated **$500 million** of fully ramped annual run-rate savings by the end of 2027. [[5]] Those benefits did not become acquisition benefits because the shareholder vote failed and the agreement was terminated; CoreWeave therefore remains a partner rather than Core Scientific’s owner. [[2]]
